Welcome to Falkland Primary School
It is with great pleasure and an absolute privilege to serve as your child’s headteacher at Falkland Primary, where your child's educational journey will be both enriching and rewarding.
At Falkland, we foster a vibrant and nurturing environment where pupils and staff create lifelong memories together, cultivating a deep love for learning. Our school thrives on imagination, creativity, enthusiasm, sportsmanship, risk-taking and the willingness to embrace challenges. Our core values of Kindness, Honesty, Reflectiveness, Resourcefulness, Resilience, and Teamwork are interwoven into every aspect of school life, ensuring a holistic and fulfilling educational experience. Childhood is a very special time, and we are committed to making it as happy and magical as possible for all of the children in our care.Kavash Bamfield | Headteacher
As a parent at Falkland, I feel incredibly grateful and reassured knowing my children are in such a warm, nurturing environment. They feel safe, supported, and genuinely inspired each day by staff who not only care deeply but challenge them to be their very best. The new headteacher’s vision has brought fresh energy and purpose to the school, and we are overjoyed to witness the wonderful, positive changes unfolding. Pupils’ voices are valued! The introduction of Pupil Voice leaders has been a game changer at Falkland. The Falkland family spirit is so real—it’s woven into every interaction, and it’s clear the values here truly shape everything our children do. This school isn’t just preparing them for secondary school; it’s helping them grow into kind, confident, and respectful young people who will bring value and compassion to those around them.Parent of a child in year 4 and year 5

Breakfast and After School Clubs
Welcome to our Breakfast club and Afterschool club! We are looking forward to seeing the children at the start of the new year and providing a warm welcome to all our families.
Click to meet the team!
Breakfast Club
Breakfast Club will take place each morning in the sports hall and is open to all year groups. Due to the planned building work beginning in September, we kindly ask that parents access the school via the Early Years gate and walk around the playground walkway to the Sports hall during this period.
Breakfast will be served daily and will include a selection of cereal, toast, fruit and yoghurt giving children a nutritious and energising start to the day.
Afterschool Club
Afterschool Club will run across both school halls:
All children will be collected from the main school reception unless parents have made prior arrangements to collect their child directly from their specific hall.
A healthy snack will be provided daily between 3.45 and 4.15pm, in line with the National Healthy Food Guidelines for EYFS Click here for further information and the Eatwell Guide . All allergies and dietary needs will be carefully accounted for. Please see below examples of afternoon snacks that could be offered:
Afterschool snacks example menu
Wyvern Club will offer a wide range of engaging activities, including:
Weekly themed craft
Games and free play
Access to outdoor spaces, weather permitting
Gardening in our Eco garden
Medication
If your child requires medication such as an inhaler or EpiPen, we kindly ask that you provide a spare set specifically for Wyvern Club. These will be stored securely and readily accessible, as school-day medication is often locked away and not immediately available after hours.
If you have any further questions please speak to Mrs Arnold (Club Leader) via email at : wyvernclub@falkland.w-berks.sch.uk

We are Linguists (French) and Cultural Explorers
We are learning. We are growing. We are Falkland.
At Falkland Primary School, we believe that learning a foreign language is an opening to other cultures which fosters pupils’ curiosity and helps deepen their understanding of the multi-cultural world we live in. We have chosen to deliver our French learning with the support of the ‘Language Angels’ scheme of work. This offers the children a high quality, challenging curriculum based on the four key areas: speaking, listening, reading and writing, which we believe will inspire and excite our pupils through a wide variety of topics whilst meeting the National Curriculum requirements. Our intention at Falkland is that by Year 6, children will be confident to hold a short conversation in French and read and write simple sentences and short paragraphs.
As you can see in our Curriculum overview document, we introduce simple songs and greetings as early as EYFS and Year 1, even though MFL is not compulsory until Year 3. We feel this solid foundation will better equip our pupils to access French at secondary school and beyond. More detail of how children progress, can be seen in our Progression of skills in French document.

We hope that our Falkland values inspire our children to adopt positive values in their lives so that they can strive to be the best people that they can be and actively demonstrate these values in their daily lives, thereby helping to create a sustainable world. We hope that our Falkland values influence our actions and attitudes, and guide us through life in all that we do and influence our relationship with ourselves and others in a positive manner.

We are Musicians
We are learning. We are growing. We are Falkland.
At Falkland, we believe that music is a powerful medium which is accessible for children of all abilities and backgrounds. It is proven that music has numerous benefits for supporting children’s emotional health and well-being. Music has the power to foster connections within the brain which will improve memory and coordination. The skills involved in playing and listening to music will also help learners develop the confidence, resilience, cooperation, creativity, and self-motivation necessary for success. We aim to establish a lifelong passion for music as an art form that is accessible to all. There is no need for specialist skills nor background knowledge to listen to and appreciate music. It is an art form that is entwined into the fabric of our lives and we aim to enable children to enrich their experience of all types of music. It is our vision that every child adopts an understanding and love of music which they can carry with them for the rest of their lives.

Falkland Clubs
At Falkland Primary, we are dedicated to nurturing the whole child and helping every pupil grow into a confident, compassionate, and responsible young person. Although our usual extensive club provision is currently paused due to limited space during the building works for our new facilities, we continue to prioritise opportunities that support curiosity, resilience, and a love of learning within the school day.

Admissions
Our admissions authority is West Berkshire Local Authority, which means that they handle all enquiries and allocations. They can be contacted on 01635 551111.
If you have a child coming up to age 5, then you must make arrangements for your child’s education. We hope you will choose Falkland Primary School. The first step is to ring the school on 01365 44949 to arrange a visit or tour. To make an application for admission you will then need to complete the West Berkshire Admissions form online or return it to West Berkshire Council’s Admissions Department.
West Berkshire’s admissions arrangements are that all children who will be turning five years old during the coming academic year may start in Early Years (Reception) full-time at the beginning of that year. For further details about our admission and appeal arrangements please contact West Berkshire Council’s Admissions department.
If you are moving into the area you will need to contact West Berkshire Council’s Admissions department who will send you a ‘Parents’ Guide to Admissions to Primary School in West Berkshire’. If a place is available you will be notified by West Berkshire Council who will then advise you of the starting date.

We are artists
We are learning. We are growing. We are Falkland.
At Falkland, we firmly believe that ‘every child is an artist’ and therefore should be given the opportunity to be inspired by great artists and to learn the skills they need to express themselves creatively. Whilst doing this, we want children to learn about the key skills associated with drawing, painting, sculpting, printmaking and digital art. We believe it is important that children are taught the correct vocabulary to describe, respond, evaluate and criticise their own work and that of the artist they are studying.
Each year, children will study a diverse range of artists which should provide them with the inspiration to express themselves creatively. Each unit of work will include a focus on improving specific art skills, knowledge about an artist and art movement and a final piece of art work. Through our robust Art and Design Curriculum, our aim is to enable our pupils to leave our school with a keen interest in Art. We aim to prepare them to express themselves creatively and to equip them with the knowledge and skills needed to succeed in studying Art and Design in secondary school and beyond.
